method: Aggregated from each unit's loci.modern_secondary array (plus cluster_citations and interlocutors where the modern_secondary entry was incomplete). A 'key figure' is a non-cluster modern scholar cited by ≥1 cluster unit. Tier-A = cited by ≥3 cluster units; Tier-B = cited by 1-2 cluster units. Figures are organized by intellectual camp in the markdown companion. Citations to within-cluster authors (Nussbaum, White, Frede, Caston, O'Gorman, González, Hawhee, Papachristou) are excluded — those are tracked in citation-network.json.

key_figures.name: Jakob Freudenthal
works_cited: Ueber den Begriff des Wortes ΦΑΝΤΑΣΙΑ bei Aristoteles (Göttingen 1863)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Foundational 1863 philological study; ancestor of 'mere show' reading González attributes to Nussbaum; gently corrected by Caston (fn. 9), approvingly cited by Frede on generalization through thinking-activity.

key_figures.name: Malcolm Schofield
works_cited: 'Aristotle on the Imagination' in Lloyd & Owen eds., Aristotle on Mind and the Senses (Cambridge 1978; reprinted 1979 Articles on Aristotle vol. 4; reprinted 1992 in Nussbaum & Rorty Essays on De Anima)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: The 'loose-knit family concept' and 'sceptical cautious phainetai' reading is the cluster's most common polemical target. Caston explicitly contests at fn. 70; Frede rejects as 'one-sided.' O'Gorman endorses with modification.

key_figures.name: Michael V. Wedin
key_figures.discipline: analytic philosophy of mind / ancient philosophy
works_cited: Mind and Imagination in Aristotle (New Haven 1988)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Wedin's 1988 monograph is the cluster's most technically refined analytic phantasia reading. Frede aligns approvingly ('reaches similar results but much more extensive'); Caston dissents at fn. 49 on phantasia as condition of sensation of proper perceptibles; González treats as key-ally.

key_figures.name: Deborah K. W. Modrak
works_cited: 'ΦΑΝΤΑΣΙΑ Reconsidered' AGPh 68 (1986)
Aristotle: The Power of Perception (Chicago 1987)
Aristotle's Theory of Language and Meaning (2001)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Principal polemical foil for both Frede and Caston. Modrak's 'belief-like character' / unified-concept-of-consciousness reading is rejected by Caston (fns. 7, 39, 48, 55) and by Frede (fns. 5, 10, 42, 44, 48). Hawhee pairs Modrak with Caston on the ill fit of 'imagination'; Papachristou cites neutrally.

key_figures.name: W. D. Ross
works_cited: Aristotle, De Anima (Oxford 1961)
Aristotle (Methuen, 5th ed. 1961a; rep. Routledge 1995)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: The standard mid-century commentary. Nussbaum contests Ross's collage-of-pictures reading at 434a7-10. Frede inverts Ross's verdict that phantasia is a 'disability.' Cited by all DA-focused units.

key_figures.name: Gerard Watson
works_cited: 'ΦΑΝΤΑΣΙΑ in Aristotle De Anima 3.3' Classical Quarterly 32 (1982)
Phantasia in Classical Thought (Galway 1988)
'The Concept of Phantasia from the Late Hellenistic Period to Early Neoplatonism' ANRW II.36.7 (1994)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: The standard reference for post-Aristotelian phantasia history. Frede engages on anti-Platonic stance and physiology; Watson 1988 is Caston's main pointer to later Hellenistic phantasia.

key_figures.name: D. A. Rees
works_cited: 'Aristotle's Treatment of ΦΑΝΤΑΣΙΑ' in Anton & Kustas eds., Essays in Ancient Greek Philosophy (Albany 1971), 491-504
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Mid-century binary propositional/imagistic gloss; cited as background by Caston (fn. 1), as foil by Nussbaum (pp. 492-93). Standard literature-review reference.

key_figures.name: Joyce Engmann
works_cited: 'Imagination and Truth in Aristotle' Journal of the History of Philosophy 14 (1976), 259-65
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Caston cites approvingly at fn. 67 as antecedent of the broader (non-propositional) falsity reading.

key_figures.name: K. Lycos
works_cited: 'Aristotle and Plato on "Appearing"' Mind 73 (1964), 496-514
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Earlier appearance/belief-sensation analysis cited at Caston fn. 54; Nussbaum and White both invoke for Aristotelian/Platonic phantasia continuity.

key_figures.name: Jean-Louis Labarrière
works_cited: 'Imagination humaine et imagination animale chez Aristote' Phronesis 29 (1984), 17-49
'L'orateur politique face à ses contraintes' (1994)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Specialist on animal vs. human phantasia. Background-cited by Caston; key-ally and rare-dissenter for González.

key_figures.name: Richard Sorabji
key_figures.discipline: King's College London / Aristotelian commentary tradition
works_cited: Aristotle on Memory (London 1972)
'Body and Soul in Aristotle' (1974)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Sorabji's 1972 Aristotle on Memory is the image-theorist par excellence. Nussbaum positions phantasia-in-action against Sorabji's mnemonic image-theory; Frede cites for physiology and integrative-nous; O'Gorman 'corrects' Sorabji on the memory connection.

key_figures.name: R. D. Hicks
works_cited: Aristotle, De anima (Cambridge 1907; rep. Arno 1976)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Canonical philological DA commentary. Nussbaum and Caston engage on individual passages (Caston fn. 8 and fn. 13 on punctuation); voice-image reading rejected by Nussbaum.

key_figures.name: D. W. Hamlyn
works_cited: Aristotle's De Anima Books II and III (Clarendon 1968)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Standard Clarendon translation. Frede notes Hamlyn as 'cryptic' on plurality of senses and number; Nussbaum engages on 431a8 and 431b17.

key_figures.name: Myles Burnyeat
works_cited: The Theaetetus of Plato (Indianapolis 1990), pp. 7-65
(1981) on intellectual habituation
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Caston relies on Burnyeat's Theaetetus reading for Platonic-Secret-Doctrine background and the mutual implication of theses A and B (fn. 22); acknowledged in closing. Frede cites supportively for residual epistemic gap between empirical generalization and nous of first principles.

key_figures.name: George A. Kennedy
works_cited: On Rhetoric: A Theory of Civic Discourse (Oxford UP translation, 1991/2007 2nd ed.)
'Reworking Aristotle's Rhetoric' in Johnstone ed. (1996)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: The standard Aristotle Rhetoric translator and the rhetoric subcluster's methodological anchor. O'Gorman and Hawhee both deploy Kennedy's 1991 translation; Hawhee additionally cites the 1996 reworking essay.

key_figures.name: William W. Fortenbaugh
works_cited: Aristotle on Emotion (1975; 2nd ed. 2002)
'Aristotle's Platonic Attitude Toward Delivery' (1986)
'Persuasion through Character' (1996)
'Aristotle's Rhetoric on Emotions' (1974)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: The cluster's authority on Aristotle's pathē in the Rhetoric. Rhetoric-subcluster authors all engage Fortenbaugh's emotion theory as background for phantasia-pathē linkage.

key_figures.name: David Konstan
works_cited: The Emotions of the Ancient Greeks (Toronto 2007)
Emotions in Context: Aristotle's Treatment of the Passions in the Rhetoric and His Moral Psychology (1996)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Konstan's emotion-theory work backstops González's and Hawhee's pathē/phantasia analyses; principal modern interlocutor for Aristotelian-affective-cognition outside the analytic DA literature.

key_figures.name: H. A. Wolfson
works_cited: 'The Internal Senses in Latin, Arabic and Hebrew Philosophical Texts' Harvard Theological Review 28 (1935)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: 1935 history-of-ideas piece on the internal-senses tradition. White uses Wolfson as authority for the post-Aristotelian Galenic genealogy at fn. 4; Hawhee cites the same article for the Latin-Arabic-Hebrew transmission.

key_figures.name: M. W. Bundy
works_cited: The Theory of Imagination in Classical and Medieval Thought (Urbana 1927)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Standard 1927 history-of-imagination handbook. Background reference for the longue-durée trajectory; both White and Caston cite without engaging.

key_figures.name: Kenneth Turnbull
works_cited: 'De Anima iii 3' in Gerson ed. Aristotle: Critical Assessments Vol. I (1999); 'Aristotle on Imagination: De anima iii 3' Ancient Philosophy 14 (1994)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Cited among the 'visual reading' camp at O'Gorman n. 6; cited as indicative reading by Papachristou.

key_figures.name: D. Gallop
works_cited: Aristotle On Sleep and Dreams (Warminster: Aris & Phillips 1996)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: The standard De Insomniis / De Somno translation. Caston fn. 66; Papachristou for Parva Naturalia.

key_figures.name: G. E. L. Owen
works_cited: 'Tithenai ta phainomena' in Mansion ed. Aristote et les problèmes de méthode (Louvain 1961)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Nussbaum's thesis supervisor at Harvard and Oxford; methodological anchor for the 'tithenai ta phainomena' approach. Caston invokes at fn. 42 for predecessor-views methodology.

key_figures.name: Charles Kahn
works_cited: 'Sensation and Consciousness in Aristotle' (1966)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Frede aligns with Kahn on confining unity-of-consciousness to the inner sense rather than extending it to intellect; key alliance for Frede's anti-Modrak argument.

key_figures.name: S. Cashdollar
works_cited: 'Aristotle's Account of Incidental Perception' Phronesis 18 (1973), 156-75
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Caston cites approvingly at fn. 48 against Modrak and Wedin on incidental perception; Frede engages on perceptive predication and habit.

key_figures.name: Cornelius Castoriadis
works_cited: The Imaginary Institution of Society (trans. Blamey, MIT Press 1998 [1975])
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Papachristou invokes Castoriadis for the continental imaginary-tradition framing of Aristotelian phantasia; the cluster's main bridge to post-phenomenological imagination theory.

key_figures.name: Martin Heidegger
works_cited: (via Spiegelberg, The Phenomenological Movement)
key_figures.role_in_cluster: White invokes Heidegger as part of the modern continental phantasia genealogy (Leibniz, Kant, Hegel, Husserl, Heidegger at fn. 11); cross-pipeline anchor to Heidegger GA 18 reading of pathos as phantasia-correlate.

key_figures.name: Immanuel Kant
works_cited: Critique of Pure Reason A 190ff; B 154
key_figures.role_in_cluster: Frede invokes Kant explicitly at two crucial junctures: synthesis of manifold (§II, A 190ff = looking up/down a house) and Gestalt requirement for thought (§III, B 154 = cannot think a line without drawing one). The cluster's most prominent post-Aristotelian philosophical parallel.
